title: ClassAnalyzer
question: What should an overlay show when it loses a classroom track?
summary: In this synthetic classroom sequence, Track 01 is still unmatched four seconds into a 30-second alert. The countdown reads 26 seconds.
role: I contributed cross-platform CI to the ClassAnalyzer repository.
collaborators: ClassAnalyzer project team (tracking overlay and classroom prototype)

provenance.scope: Project scope and intended processing model.
Cross-platform CI changes under Subhasis’s public GitHub account.
Tracking IDs, missing-track countdown, and recovery on a match.

decision.title: Keep the gap visible
decision.description: Keep the last tracked ID on screen and show how long the alert has left. Clear it when a matching detection returns. The visible state describes what the tracker observed and leaves the cause of the gap open for review.

caseStudy.limitation: Tracking IDs and countdowns are model observations. A gap could reflect occlusion, someone moving out of frame, or a tracking error. The example uses fictional data.
caseStudy.learning: A countdown gives a reviewer a place to look in the session. The missing state can reflect occlusion, movement out of frame, or a tracking error. Track state alone provides no basis for judging attendance, attention, or engagement.
